newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt lower as concerns of Dow, FOMC linger.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt lower as concerns of Dow, FOMC linger.

text.p: Brady bond prices were lower on Monday on concerns about U.S. stock prices and nervousness ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday, market experts said.
But some market specialists said fundamentals were still largely unchanged and could thus prompt investors to buy on any further weakness.
Still, they said trading activity was likely to remain thin ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday though expectations for a U.S. interest rate hike remained slim.

"I would say people are looking at what happens at the Dow Jones and if there are any further signs of weakness that could affect the Brady market," said Chris Portman, senior economist at ANZ Investment Bank.
But Portman added: "Once we get past the New York trading session today, I think we will see some stability in the market and some buyers coming back in."
Peter West, chief economist at BBV Latinvest, said: "People will be looking at the Dow today and the FOMC tomorrow but perhaps when we get over that prices will begin to steady."
Traders said continued concerns about turmoil in the Asian currency markets added to the bearish tone today in the Brady bond market.
"People are pretty concerned about continued instability with the Asian currencies. This whole environment is not very good for the market," one trader at a major European bank said.
In the Latin Brady market, Mexican Brady bonds suffered the sharpest losses on news that the brother of the country's finance minister Guillermo Ortiz had been killed in Mexico City over the weekend.
"The Finance Minister's brother getting shot has apparently created some nervousness in the market. Spreads have widened a bit this morning on the back of that," said West.
Mexican Pars MX625L19=RR were 5/8 weaker at 80-1/8 bid and the country's discount bonds MXFLL19=RR were 3/4 lower at 94 bid.
Elsewhere, investors were expected to focus on Brazil's current account figures for July later today and on the country's fiscal numbers for June on Tuesday.
"Those are important pieces of informattion...and obviously they will be analysed very closely," West said.
In the broader sector of the market, traders said prices remained lower.
Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were 1/2 weaker at 101-1/8 and Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 7/8 lower at 77-7/8 bid. -- Diane Craft, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5110
